# Checklist: security
<!-- Generated by /hef.checklist -->
<!-- Branch: feature/007-onboarding-de-orgs | Date: 2026-09-27 -->

This feature adds a **seventh enumerated consumer of the system client** — `overrideAccess: true`
on a maker's upload — and a creation path for the collection that **is** the tenant. Two rows below
are tenant-resolution defects that exist **today**, before any line of 007 is written, and which a
wizard would make easy to trigger.

| ID | Check | Dimension | Ref | Status |
|----|-------|-----------|-----|--------|
| CHK020 | Does the wizard's gate read the **global** role? `tech-stack.md`: *"identity is global, role is per organization; `master` is a global role."* A check on a per-organization membership role would admit an org admin, or refuse a master who belongs to no organization. T026 names the exact field path and tests both directions | [authorization] | FR-009, D1, T026 | [ ] |
| CHK021 | Does the view refuse **before any data read**? The `notFound()` must be the first statement in the server component. A refusal after a fetch has already put the data into a rendered payload | [authorization] | FR-009, T026 | [ ] |
| CHK022 | Does FR-018's "not widened" assertion cover **every surface**? T021 as written tests the Local API. `organizations` is also reachable through REST (`/api/organizations/:id`) and GraphQL. An org admin must be refused on all three | [authorization] | FR-018, CLR-005, T021 | [ ] |
| CHK023 | Does D7's projection keep the promise it exists for? **No.** Sketch 8 projects `theme: true` — the **whole group** — which serves `theme.logoUrl`, `theme.heroImageUrl` and any theme field added later to anonymous visitors. That is the exact failure D7 claims to prevent: a column becoming public by being declared. Project `theme.primaryColor` explicitly — which needs a nested select type (see CHK030) | [data-protection] | FR-017, D7, T017 | ✗ found |
| CHK024 | **Confused deputy.** `getOrganizationUsageStore(tenantId)` runs with `overrideAccess: true` on a tenant id taken from `data.tenant` — a value from the request body or the admin's cookie. Can a maker put **another organization's id** in `tenant` and charge B's quota, or evade A's? T005 must prove the plugin **rejects** a foreign `tenant` **before** the quota hook reads it. Otherwise the seventh door reads a caller-chosen tenant with no access control | [authorization] | FR-022, FR-034, T005, T008 | [ ] |
| CHK025 | If CHK024 fails, the refusal message itself **discloses another organization's usage and quota** to the uploader. The message test must run with a foreign `tenant` in the body as well as a correct one | [data-protection] | FR-034, T013 | [ ] |
| CHK026 | **Tenant hijack by slug, on the current tree.** `lookupOrganizationByHost` step 1 matches `slug = <first host label>` **OR** `domains.domain = <hostname>`, with `limit: 1` and **no sort** (`lib/tenancy/resolve.ts`). A new organization whose slug equals another organization's first domain label — `localhost` in development, `cite` against a `cite.unesp.br` domain — makes two rows match, and Postgres picks one arbitrarily. FR-003 must refuse a slug equal to the first label of any domain any organization declares, plus reserved labels (`www`, `admin`, `api`) | [input-sanitization] | FR-003, FR-004, T025 | ✗ found |
| CHK027 | **Tenant hijack by domain, on the current tree.** `organizations_domains` has **no unique index** on `domain` (queried: only the primary key, `_order` and `_parent_id` indexes exist). Two organizations can declare the same host today, and resolution picks one arbitrarily — the same query as CHK026. The wizard's domain step would make it one form field away. Needs a cross-organization uniqueness check **and** a unique index, or two concurrent saves still both succeed | [input-sanitization] | FR-002, FR-011, T026 | ✗ found |
| CHK028 | Does the first-administrator step keep `tech-stack.md`'s promise — an invite to an existing e-mail *"adds a membership, never creates an account, never reveals the account exists in another org"*? The wizard's success and failure messages must read the same whether or not the e-mail already exists | [authentication] | FR-010, T027 | [ ] |
